LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
This PKGBUILD file is a standard packaging script for the OpenZFS `zfs-linux-lts` and `zfs-linux-lts-headers` packages on Arch Linux. The analysis covers several security concerns:

**Source integrity**: The package downloads its source from the official OpenZFS GitHub releases (`https://github.com/openzfs/zfs/releases/download/zfs-${_zfsver}/zfs-${_zfsver}.tar.gz`), which is the expected upstream location. A specific SHA256 checksum (`2a3c70d55a37cc71618a95a60e81ad66530201eb118d37741dc92efcf848c8b1`) is provided (not `SKIP`), enabling verification of the downloaded tarball. The kernel version (`6.18.47-1`) and ZFS version (`2.4.4`) are hardcoded as variables, and the `makedepends`/`depends` arrays pin these to the exact kernel version, ensuring ABI compatibility.

**Build process**: The `build()` function runs `autogen.sh`, `configure`, and `make` using the kernel headers at `/usr/lib/modules/${_extramodules}/build`. This is the standard and expected build process for out-of-tree kernel modules on Arch Linux. No unusual or obfuscated commands are present — no `eval`, `base64`, `curl`, `wget`, or any runtime network activity. No `git pull`, `git fetch`, or `git reset --hard` is used, so the build relies solely on the verified source tarball.

**Package installation**: Both `package_zfs-linux-lts()` and `package_zfs-linux-lts-headers()` perform standard installation via `make DESTDIR=... install`. The `rm -r` commands remove source build artifacts from the package directory (e.g., `${pkgdir}/usr/src`, `${pkgdir}/lib`), which is routine. The `sed -i "s+${srcdir}++"` command sanitizes absolute build paths from `Module.symvers`, a common reproducibility/hygiene practice. No files outside `${pkgdir}` are modified, no system-wide configuration is altered beyond standard kernel module packaging, and no post-install scripts install services or modify system security posture.

No evidence of malicious behavior was found. The file is consistent with legitimate AUR packaging practices.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>
Standard OpenZFS PKGBUILD with verified upstream source, no malicious content</summary>
</security_assessment>
